headline: Apple unveils new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 chip, boosting AI and graphics
summary: The M6 chip brings a 12-core CPU, 12-core GPU, and enhanced AI capabilities, delivering up to 24 hours of battery life. Graphics are 30% faster than M5, with pre-orders starting Oct 28.
details: Apple has officially announced the new 14-inch MacBook Pro, powered by the M6 chip. This update brings significant performance enhancements, advanced on-device AI capabilities, and improved connectivity, targeting students, business users, and creative professionals. It promises up to 24 hours of battery life.

The M6 chip features an advanced 12-core CPU, boasting the world’s fastest CPU core for incredibly fast and responsive performance across all tasks. Its 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads compared to the M5 chip.

Users upgrading from an M1-powered MacBook Pro will see even more dramatic improvements, with up to 11x faster graphics and 13x faster AI performance. The M6 also includes additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, making it a powerful platform for AI tasks.

This enhanced AI capability supports features like Siri AI, Apple Intelligence across macOS, and the ability to run large language models (LLMs) locally while maintaining user privacy. The new MacBook Pro also includes Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 for faster wireless connectivity.

Other advanced features include a stunning Liquid Retina XDR display with an optional nano-texture finish, a 12MP Center Stage camera, and an immersive six-speaker sound system. It also offers a wide array of ports for versatile connectivity.
The new 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 is available in space black and silver finishes. Pre-orders begin tomorrow, October 28, with general availability starting on Friday, November 6.

headline: Apple Creator Studio gets AI and MotionVFX updates for Final Cut Pro and more
summary: Apple's Creator Studio suite receives significant updates, integrating MotionVFX tools into Final Cut Pro and introducing new AI capabilities across Logic Pro, Pixelmator Pro, Keynote, Pages, and Numbers, some powered by OpenAI.
details: Apple has updated its Creator Studio software suite, integrating MotionVFX tools into Final Cut Pro and adding AI features across multiple apps. This follows Apple's acquisition of MotionVFX earlier this year.

The MotionVFX integration provides editors with rapid access to extensive professional video effects and content, including graphics, themes, titles, transitions, rotoscoping, and color grading tools. A new Content Hub also offers curated stock videos, photos, and backgrounds.

Workflow improvements allow images from Final Cut Pro timelines to be opened directly in Pixelmator Pro for edits, with changes applied instantly to the original project. Users can now also disconnect clips from the primary timeline in Final Cut Pro.

AI is now present across Apple's apps, with text-to-image generation and editing tools in Final Cut Pro and Pixelmator Pro. In Pixelmator Pro, users can prompt AI to apply specific edits by drawing a circle over an image area.

Logic Pro features a new OpenAI-powered assistant for editing existing projects, starting new songs, and generating vocal tracks from text prompts. The same chatbot assists in Keynote, Pages, and Numbers for tasks like animating slides or organizing data.

Other quality-of-life additions include advanced keyframe easing in Final Cut Pro and the Stem Splitter in Logic Pro for isolating or swapping drum parts. These updates will be available for free to existing subscribers in November.

Apple Creator Studio costs $13 per month or $129 per year, with a one-month free trial for new subscribers. Individual apps like Final Cut Pro ($300), Logic Pro ($200), and Pixelmator Pro ($50) can also be purchased separately.

Some features require specific hardware and software, such as an Apple Intelligence-supported Mac running macOS 27 Golden Gate for the Logic Pro assistant, or Apple silicon for certain Final Cut Pro features.
